title: Language, Caste, and Context: Demographic Disparities in AI-Generated Explanations Across Indian and American STEM Educational Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with intersectional student profiles containing varying income levels (high, middle, low) and measuring the linguistic complexity (Mean Grade Level) and recommended difficulty (Mean Choice Value) of generated STEM explanations.

Constructing Indian student profiles with different caste identities (General, OBC, SC, ST) and evaluating disparities in the difficulty and grade level of personalized educational explanations using Mean Absolute Bias (MAB) and Maximum Difference Bias (MDB) metrics.

Generating American student profiles with diverse racial/ethnic identities (White, Black, Hispanic, Native American) and assessing the complexity of AI-generated tutoring explanations assigned to each group.
Comparing the instructional complexity assigned by LLMs to Indian student profiles designated as studying in English-medium versus Hindi/Regional-medium educational instruction.

Varying the educational institutional affiliation (e.g., HBCU, Ivy League, IIT, community college) and school type (e.g., public, private, charter) in student prompts to measure differential treatment in the depth and complexity of educational support.
Testing LLM outputs for student profiles with different gender identities (Male, Female, Non-binary) to measure variations in assigned explanation difficulty and complexity.
Modifying the geographic location of student profiles (Metro, Tier-2, Rural for India; Urban, Suburban, Rural for the US) to evaluate disparities in the complexity of generated math explanations.
